errors.claim: The appropriate response should differ according to the circumstances in which the error was made rather than the outcome that occurred.
errors.source_check: The source says the response can and should differ according to the circumstances in which an error was made; outcome, result, and consequence are absent.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to the appropriate response can and should differ according to the circumstances in which an error was made

errors.claim: The foresight and substitution tests together account for four of the seven recommendation end-states.
errors.source_check: Q3 exits only to Recommendation D and Q4 exits only to Recommendation E, so the two tests account for two distinct end-states.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to the foresight and substitution tests together account for two of the seven recommendation end-states

errors.claim: The foresight and substitution branches route by default to not singling out the individual.
searches: unlikely to be appropriate|not appropriate to single out
errors.source_check: Recommendations D and E say action singling out the individual is unlikely to be appropriate and add that wider actions may include the individual.
errors.suggested_fix: add qualifier that singling out the individual is unlikely to be appropriate and that wider actions may include the individual

errors.source_check: The summary preserves the caveats' meaning but condenses the first caveat and rephrases the fourth; as a group it is not essentially verbatim.

errors.claim: At any test, a positive finding exits to a recommendation and a negative finding proceeds to the next test.
errors.source_check: Q3 reverses that polarity: Yes to all three proceeds to Q4 and No to any exits to D. Q5 has no next test; both answers exit.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to each answer routes either to an exit recommendation or to the next test, with the direction varying by test

errors.claim: The source treats impaired-capacity contributors as conditions for health or substance-abuse guidance, not as individual culpability.
searches: substance abuse at work guidance|health issues affecting work|occupational health
errors.source_check: The source routes Q2 findings to substance-abuse-at-work or health guidance and wider investigation, but it does not use the concepts of impaired capacity or culpability.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to Q2 routes these findings to the relevant organisational health or substance-abuse-at-work guidance and wider investigation

errors.claim: A No at any foresight sub-question means the locus of the problem is upstream of the individual.
errors.source_check: The source says singling out the individual is unlikely to be appropriate and that wider actions may include the individual; it does not locate the problem wholly upstream.
errors.suggested_fix: add qualifier that wider investigation should identify the needed actions and that those actions may include the individual

errors.claim: Any positive substitution-test finding routes to system-level corrective action rather than individual management action.
errors.source_check: Recommendation E prioritises wider investigation and says singling out is unlikely to be appropriate, but expressly allows the wider actions to include the individual.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to any positive finding routes to wider investigation; singling out is unlikely to be appropriate, but actions may include the individual

errors.claim: Recommendations D, E, and F route away from management action directed at the individual.
searches: Recommendation [DEF]|unlikely to be appropriate|may not be appropriate
errors.source_check: D and E say singling out is unlikely to be appropriate. F only says individual-directed action may not be appropriate and calls for senior HR advice on the degree of mitigation.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to D and E route away from singling out, while F leaves individual-directed action conditional on the degree of mitigation

errors.claim: The B and C health-affecting-work pathways are themselves not punitive.
searches: substance abuse at work guidance|health issues affecting work|occupational health
errors.source_check: Recommendations B and C prescribe organisational guidance, occupational-health referral where likely, and wider investigation; the source does not characterise these pathways as non-punitive.

errors.claim: Recommendations D and E apply the same default response when an exoneration arises from either the foresight or substitution test.
errors.source_check: D and E are textually identical, but they say singling out is unlikely to be appropriate and allow actions to include the individual; they do not describe the finding as exoneration.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to D and E apply the same qualified response when either test routes to its recommendation

errors.claim: A No to Q4c establishes that supervision was provided.
errors.source_check: Q4c asks whether senior team members failed to provide supervision that normally should be provided. A No establishes no such positive finding, not affirmatively that supervision was provided.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to there was no indication that senior team members failed to provide supervision that normally should be provided

errors.claim: Four of seven recommendation paths, B through E, route to not singling out the individual.
searches: unlikely to be appropriate|may not be appropriate|health issues affecting work|substance abuse at work
errors.source_check: Only D and E explicitly say singling out is unlikely to be appropriate. F conditionally says individual action may not be appropriate; B and C route to substance-abuse or health guidance without making a no-singling-out claim.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to two recommendations, D and E, explicitly say singling out is unlikely to be appropriate; describe B, C, and F separately
